clue.text: Chilean ready to eat starter of tomato sauce

indicators.note: the currency swallows the letter, so it sits inside

parts.note: the peso is Chile's currency, and ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone from Chile is about to tuck into a tomato sauce as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilean' looks like a person; with 'ready' (British slang for money) it is Chile's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is the Genoese basil-and-pine-nut paste served as a pasta sauce.

clue.text: Complex theatre work? I'm only a GP getting trained!

indicators.note: being trained reshapes the letters into a new form

parts.note: these letters, rearranged, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor protests that, as a mere GP, they are out of their depth with this difficult play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shaw's play Eliza is trained to speak like a lady, echoing the indicator. A Pygmalion complex is also a psychological term.
explanation.definitionFit: Pygmalion is George Bernard Shaw's play, and the name also labels a psychological complex of falling for one's own creation.

clue.text: Sawbones amputating leg that's swelling

indicators.note: amputating cuts off a part, taking those letters away

parts.note: a sawbones is old slang for a surgeon
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes a leg because of a swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rise or welling-up, as of water or a crowd.

clue.text: Homesickness leaving Poles nagging pain

indicators.note: the poles leave, so their letters are removed

parts.note: nostalgia originally meant homesickness
N and S, the north and south poles, both go: N from the front and S from the middle

explanation.surface: Pining for home after quitting Poland brings a persistent ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical word for earache, and nagging is what gives a person earache.

clue.text: Sore swelling caused by poor Bill being shackled?

parts.note: shackled means held in a chain, so the word for that restraint wraps around the jumbled name

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of the name are in a bad way and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor Bill, kept in irons, has developed a sore from the chafing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilblain is an itchy, painful inflammation of the skin caused by cold.

clue.text: Companion's "Phwoar!" occasionally in bed?

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some letters, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters are taken

explanation.surface: A partner's appreciative exclamation now and then while in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Phwoar is British slang expressing lustful admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort can mean a supporter or companion, as in a crony or sidekick.

clue.text: Angel wearing singlet, gold

parts.note: if you are wearing a garment you are in it
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, a singlet
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An angel dressed in a vest with a golden glow.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre an angel is someone who puts money into a production.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical angel is a financial backer who funds a show, so a backer of money.

clue.text: Sheepish sound, with one supporting the video ref intervening where Bayern play

indicators.note: intervening puts these letters into the bleat

parts.note: baa is a sheep's bleat

indicators.note: in a down clue one under another holds it up, so it comes after

parts.note: VAR is the video assistant referee in football
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sheepish noise from a footballer as a VAR decision comes into play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like embarrassed but means made by a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayern Munich is a football club in Munich, the capital of the German state of Bavaria.

clue.text: Vegetable soup of haricot and kale, cored

indicators.note: a soup is a mixture, so the letters are blended

parts.note: taken whole as part of the mix

indicators.note: cored removes the middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters survive the coring

explanation.surface: A vegetable soup made with haricot beans and kale with the stems removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Material transatlantic route shortened?

indicators.note: shortened cuts the end off

parts.note: New York to London, NY-LONDON, crosses the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Is a quicker flight across the Atlantic something material?
explanation.walkthrough: A popular myth says the fabric's name comes from New York plus London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre used to make fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: A piece from Grieg or Bach evoking an instrumental figure

indicators.note: a piece taken out of the run of words, so the answer lies inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Grieg, through 'or Bach', into the start of evoking

explanation.surface: Music by Grieg or Bach conjures up a figure played on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental' suggests music; here it means helpful in bringing something about, as the Soviet leader was in ending the Cold War.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Gorbachev was the leader instrumental in ending the Cold War and the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Invigorating bottled Tango

parts.note: bottled read as put in a small bottle, a vial, so that container surrounds the letter
T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A refreshing drink of Tango, the orange soda, served from a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British fizzy orange drink, but here it is the radio code word for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital can mean full of energy and life, so something vital is enlivening.

clue.text: Reginald and Evangeline briefly reviewed Iron Man, say

indicators.note: viewed again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Reg is the usual short form of Reginald
N stands for and, as in rock 'n' roll
Eva is a shortened form of Evangeline

explanation.surface: Two critics, Reg and Evangeline, wrote short reviews of the superhero film Iron Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims both names to their pet forms; 'and' gives its usual crossword N.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Man is one of Marvel's superhero team the Avengers, so he is an example.

clue.text: Arab finds career in hospital

indicators.note: in places the speeding word inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
to career is to race headlong

explanation.surface: An Arab man finds a job in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' reads as a profession but is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim, especially at the time of the Crusades.

clue.text: Large malt with a twist guzzled? Not half!

indicators.note: a twist mixes the letters into a new order
the drink is knocked back and churned about, another sign the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Islay is a Scottish island famous for its single malt whiskies, so a malt may be named after it

explanation.surface: A big whisky with a twist of lemon, gulped down: was it good? Definitely!
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is the Hebridean island whose whiskies are known simply by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Not half! is British slang for emphatic agreement, the same exclamation as an enthusiastic you bet.

clue.text: Californian cops note my admitted impressive bit of speeding!

indicators.note: admitted lets the other letters in

parts.note: LAPD, the Los Angeles Police Department
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
cor is an exclamation like my!

explanation.surface: Pulled over by LA police, a driver confesses to some spectacular speeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap record is the fastest circuit ever driven on a racetrack, a feat of speed.

clue.text: Christian designer, American, cut back an instant 26

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A fashion designer and an American trimmed a snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a faith but is Dior's first name. 26 refers to PHOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaroid cameras produce self-developing prints within minutes, so the result is a picture taken and printed instantly.

clue.text: New in: falsely accused, papa must be daft to get fitted up with this

definitions.text: daft to get fitted up with this

indicators.note: in places the letter for new inside
falsely means the letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble
P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newcomer framed by false accusations must be foolish to be set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitted up' is British slang for framed, but here it means wearing the conical paper hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce's cap was a cone-shaped paper hat put on a slow pupil as a mark of stupidity.

clue.text: Taught here commonly spoken Spanish course

indicators.note: said in a common accent, dropping the h, the phrase is heard as the answer

parts.note: said with dropped aitch, 'taught 'ere', it is close to the Spanish dish's name

explanation.surface: A language school offering the Spanish course taught on site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a class but is a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish tortilla is a thick potato omelette served as a dish.

clue.text: Exile flying monoplane miles away

indicators.note: the letters are sent flying into a new arrangement
away tells us the letter for miles goes from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exile flees in a single-winged aircraft, many miles from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to Elba and then St Helena, the most famous exile in history.

clue.text: No ordinary Prime Minister, Johnson familiarly sent up in satire

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up reverses the letters

parts.note: taken as written
O for ordinary, as in the old O level
Boris Johnson's first name is Alexander, and family call him Al

explanation.surface: An extraordinary prime minister, Boris Johnson, is mocked in satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' also means mocked, which fits both the surface and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a mocking piece of writing ridiculing someone, a form of satire.

clue.text: Initially called time leaving pub which is popular with potholers

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: only its first letter is used

indicators.note: the time letter departs from the pub, leaving the rest

parts.note: a tavern is an inn or pub

explanation.surface: Last orders called, someone heads out of a pub much frequented by cavers.
explanation.walkthrough: Potholers are British cave explorers.
explanation.definitionFit: Potholing is the British pastime of exploring underground caves, so a large cave is a natural draw.

clue.text: A tad upset, chap goes in hard!

indicators.note: goes in puts the man inside
upset means the letters are overturned into a new order

parts.note: these four letters are jumbled
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Slightly annoyed, a fellow tackles firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, from the old word for an unbreakably hard stone.

clue.text: Spanish snack served up with heartless, haughty indifference

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means turned upwards

parts.note: a tapa is a Spanish bar snack

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, keeping the ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Tapas brought to the table by a snooty, uncaring waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, the same as not caring.

clue.text: Anticipate European politician popping into sandwich shop

indicators.note: popping into puts the pair inside the shop name

parts.note: Pret A Manger is a British chain of sandwich shops, often called Pret
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MEP-type figure drops into a sandwich bar ahead of the lunch rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Pret A Manger is a sandwich chain found on most British high streets.
explanation.definitionFit: To pre-empt something is to act first so as to forestall it, which is to anticipate it.

clue.text: City boss Yves discharged diary keeper

parts.note: Pep Guardiola, manager of Manchester City

indicators.note: discharged empties the word, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: emptied, only its outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A football boss sacks someone called Yves, who kept a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a financial district but is Manchester City football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys was the 17th-century English diarist famous for his account of the Great Fire of London.

clue.text: Chat idly about voting system with former PM endlessly

parts.note: PR is proportional representation

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee, UK Prime Minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: Gossiping about electoral reform with an ex-premier who never stops talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to talk at length in a foolish or inconsequential way, the same as babbling.

clue.text: Like Scrooge when squiffy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: miserly, like Dickens's skinflint Scrooge
second meaning: drunk; squiffy is British slang for tipsy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Scrooge drunk; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stingy with money and slightly drunk.

clue.text: Snap up hot organic wraps

indicators.note: the run of words wraps the answer, holding it inside

parts.note: the answer starts at the end of up, takes in hot, and finishes with the first letter of organic

explanation.surface: Quick, grab some warm organic wraps from the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like food but signals the answer is held in the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a quick photograph, as in a holiday snapshot.

clue.text: Like a slug chewing the garlic?

indicators.note: chewing mashes the letters into a new order

parts.note: these nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A garden slug munching through the garlic patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' is the garden pest in the surface; the definition reads it as a sluggard.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is slow and sluggish, so it is drowsy, torpid and lacking energy.

clue.text: Seated with The Sun perhaps, taking in garden before end of day

indicators.note: taking in holds the garden inside

parts.note: the sun is an example of a star
the Garden of Eden

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Sitting in the garden with The Sun newspaper until the day is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid in the surface, but in the wordplay it is the star itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes someone sitting down a lot, so it fits a posture rather than an activity.

clue.text: Total strop Trump's thrown on a regular basis

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second one

parts.note: its second and fourth letters are taken
the alternation runs on, taking its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Tally up the tantrums the former president throws, which happen all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is British slang for a sulky tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is a British phrasal verb for adding numbers, so to calculate a sum.
